title: ArtCraft 0.3.0 - an Open Source Desktop AI Art Tool, now with Gaussian Splats and World Generation. You can use this to craft your game cinematics
author: ai_art_is_art
selftext:
Hey folks, I got a really warm reception when I first announced ArtCraft here 4 months ago. I wanted to update you on a huge number of changes, improvements, and new features. 

ArtCraft, if you're not familiar, is an open source desktop tool for designing images and video with precision. It lets you use text-to-image and image-to-video, but it also comes with very powerful 2D and 3D control surfaces for precision crafting of the images you want to create. 

It's a lot like ComfyUI in that it's software you own instead of renting, but it's aimed at an artist crowd and intends to be visual and user friendly. 

ArtCraft works mostly with commercial models, but it allows you to use compute wherever you have it. You can add your OpenAI, Grok, Midjourney, and other subscriptions and API keys to take advantages of whoever provides your compute. We'll be adding FAL, local GPU, and many other providers soon. 

While you can subscribe to ArtCraft and fund development, you can use 100% of the app without paying us anything ever. 

Version 0.3.0 adds WorldLabs image-to-Gaussian Splat generation. With this, you can turn any image into a fully navigable 3d world where you can position your characters, props, and camera for precision filmmaking. This is fantastic for prototyping, storyboarding, and even making in-game cinematics and marketing material. 

It's really powerful to generate an image in MidJourney, turn that into a world, drop in some props, and then make prototype / demo videos. 

You can also import your game assets. The 3D engine supports OBJ, FBX, and GLB out of the box. You can even pose your rigged characters!

Here's our website, where you can download the latest build: 

[https://getartcraft.com/](https://getartcraft.com/)

Please give us a star on GitHub: 

[https://github.com/storytold/artcraft](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft)

If you're interested in developing this with us, please let us know. It's written in Rust and designed to be fast. 

We'd love to get your feedback. You can reach me in our Discord: 

[https://discord.gg/artcraft](https://discord.gg/artcraft)

Our team is 100% comprised of engineers and filmmakers. We're designing this as a tool for ourselves as well as other folks. We make a fun series of YouTube videos with AI, and you can check those out as well. The Grinch and Marvel videos are fun:

[https://www.youtube.com/@OfficialArtCraftStudios](https://www.youtube.com/@OfficialArtCraftStudios)

Also, in closing - we got some free cloud credits. We're passing that along as free Nano Banana Pro ("while it lasts"), so that should be a pretty compelling reason to try the app!

replies.author: ai_art_is_art
replies.body:
Kind of. I do half of my development on Linux, so I've made sure the core app works on Linux. The problem is the UI toolkit we chose is really under-performant on Linux. 

I'm planning to rewrite the frontend in 100% Bevy in the future. No javascript or html, just pure native Rust. But that'll be much later in the year. 

Right now the app uses Tauri so we can go fast and cover a lot of ground quickly. Tauri on Linux is pretty lame, sadly.

replies.author: ai_art_is_art
replies.body:
It's an app you download, and the source code is available on github. 

There's a server component that does the generations that we host (this is also open source), but you can bring your own compute - you can also log into ArtCraft with your Sora account, Grok account, Midjourney account, and many more. They're all usable within Artcraft!

I would appreciate subscription revenue, though! We'll invest that directly into building this. And it'll be 100% open forever, so you'll own it even if something happens to our team.

comments.author: DerrickBarra
comments.body:
Very cool! I sent it to some of my coworkers, props for making it open source.  
  
Could you use this tool to generate photogrammetry / gaussian splats from your renders? Or would you need to take the rendered outputs and then reverse those back into a splat file using another AI?

replies.author: ai_art_is_art
replies.body:
Thank you! 

The model that creates the splats could be invoked again on an image from a render.   
  
We're working on a way to edit splats and supply multiple reference images, so in theory you could edit the splat or improve upon it, but we don't have this working just yet.

comments.author: KitchenNovel4709
comments.body:
My name is Tom. I’m a retired video editor with about 30 years of professional experience in broadcast editing, motion graphics, and visual effects. Over the past few weeks I’ve been exploring the new generation of AI image and video tools and experimenting with different workflows for AI-assisted animation and filmmaking.

While researching scene consistency and camera control in AI animation, I came across ArtCraft and was immediately intrigued by the 3D staging and blocking approach. The LightWave-style navigation and ability to compose scenes spatially feels very natural from a production perspective.

I’ve been experimenting with combining tools like AI image generation and video animation models to build short animated sequences, and ArtCraft looks like it could be a very interesting previsualization and scene layout tool within that pipeline.

If you are ever looking for outside feedback or beta testers from a professional production background, I would be very happy to help test workflows and share observations from a filmmaker/editor perspective. I have passed experience doing beta testing for both Adobe and Boris effects. Here is some of my work.      [https://www.flickr.com/photos/200410359@N07/albums/72177720331672405](https://www.flickr.com/photos/200410359@N07/albums/72177720331672405)

I also maintain a small YouTube channel where I’ve been posting recent AI animation experiments along with some of my older broadcast and motion graphics work.

In any case, congratulations on an intriguing tool — I’m looking forward to seeing where the project goes.

Best regards,  
Tom
